key_insight: OpenCoF argues that video generation can serve as a new form of reasoning, where a model “thinks” by producing a sequence of temporally connected frames rather than text tokens. The paper focuses on making this Chain-of-Frame reasoning more reliable and useful through better supervision and model design.
problem_solved: Current video generation models are mostly trained on generic video data and do not have enough targeted supervision for reasoning-oriented tasks. As a result, they struggle to consistently express logical progression, causal steps, or multi-stage problem solving through generated video.
method: Introduces OpenCoF, a framework for learning reasoning through video generation using Chain-of-Frame supervision.
Adds more diverse and dedicated training signals so the model can better represent step-by-step reasoning in visual form.
Designs the system to encourage temporally coherent frame sequences that reflect logical consequences over time.
impact: This matters because it expands the idea of reasoning beyond text and into multimodal generation, opening a path for more interpretable and grounded AI behavior. For practitioners, it suggests a new way to evaluate and train models for reasoning tasks that unfold over time.

paper_title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
paper_authors: Xinyan Chen, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Hongsheng Li
